body.p: In the Final Office Action mailed on September 11, 2024, claims 1-16 are pending in the application; Claims 1-7 and 11 are withdrawn; Claims 1-7 and 11 stand rejected.
As set forth herein, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections and objections of the claims is respectfully requested.

p.u: Telephonic Interview with the Examiner on 10 January

body.p: A telephonic interview was conducted with the Examiner. In advance of the interview, the undersigned attorney sent an email to the Examiner with proposed claim amendments and arguments. The substance of the email is provided below:

Dear Examiner Steinberg, please find attached proposed claim amendments to be discussed in the interview on Friday at 1:00PM Mountain Time. These amendments are for the pending independent claims 8, 13 and 16. Each of these claims are proposed to be amended the same with two possible variations as follows:

p.u: wherein passive auscultation is achieved by recordin
e and no active auscultation is conducted;

body.p: The specification does not use the terms "active" or "passive ". However, use of a stethoscope or another electronic device to listen to auscultated sounds is only "passive". Active auscultation requires the use of a sound making device to then determine how auscultated sounds are affected. More specifically, in medical terms, 'passive auscultation" refers to listening to the body's natural sounds without any additional stimulation, while "active auscultation" involves intentionally creating sounds by manipulating the patient's body or using a specific technique to better hear certain sounds during a physical examination with a stethoscope; essentially, passive listening is just hearing what is naturally occurring, while active listening or active auscultation involves actively eliciting sounds to assess specific conditions.

With respect to the cited Caro reference, (US Patent Publication No. 2006/0243280) it is disagreed that this reference teaches only passive auscultation as now required in the proposed amended claims. Caro requires both active and passive auscultation to obtain a diagnosis. Paragraph [0091] in Caro clearly explains that combined "multiplexing" lung indicators from

both types of auscultation is required. The present invention only uses passive auscultation as that term is commonly defined and as defined in Caro itself See paragraph [0078] for the definition of passive auscultation. See paragraph [0025] of Caro for the definition of active auscultation. As mentioned above, active auscultation requires the introduction of an audible signal into the body of the examined patient and thereafter receiving and monitoring the signal after it has passed through the body. Caro absolutely requires the combination of both passive and active auscultation to make any diagnosis. Caro does not provide the option to select one or the other type of auscultation technique.
Please consider the foregoing in advance of our interview. Thank you.

During the interview, the proposed claim amendments were discussed. The Examiner raised a concern under Section 112 first paragraph regarding the proposed amendment using language not originally found in the specification and particularly with respect to using the terms "no active auscultation".

The Examiner suggested limiting the claims to specific structure such as the claimed stethoscope so that the stethoscope is interpreted as the only element that performs sensing of auscultated sounds.
No agreement was reached as to allowable claims.

Claims 8-10 and 13-15 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over US Patent Publication No. 2006/0201432 (hereinafter referred as Pratt) in view of US Patent Publication No. 2007/0106179 (hereinafter referred as Bagha); in view of US Patent Publication No. 2006/0243280) (hereinafter referred as Caro) further in view of US Patent Publication No. 2006/0206013) (hereinafter referred as Rothman). The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
Independent claims 8, and 13 are amended herein to recite that the device for recording auscultated lung sounds consists of a stethoscope.

Claim 17 is new and is the same as claim 8 except that the recited device for recording auscultated lung sounds consists of an audio digital recording unit. The claim covers the embodiment disclosed in the specification beginning on line 8 of page 14. As disclosed in the specification on page, 8, the audio digital recording unit is provided that has the same functionality as the digital stethoscopes described in the other embodiments, however the recording unit

provides a convenient means to record sounds through the use of a multi-channel microphone in the form of a curved paddle shaped device. The other claims in this rejected group of claims depend from claims 8 and 13 and should be considered allowable at least based on their respective dependencies.

The amendments to the independent claims and the new claim 17 are submitted in an earnest attempt to obtain allowable subject matter based on the recent telephonic interview with the Examiner. Therefore, this rejection should be reconsidered and withdrawn.
